notes.pairs: each pair is judged with a corrections store of its own, holding one override: that of its misjudged image
notes.truth: VisA's defect type under region 1, the most anomalous flagged area, read from the ground-truth mask; empty for a good board
notes.right: the judge names the class and the clause the pair expects; for a good board, that no clause applies
notes.by_part: the part's most recent corrections stand in the prompt; one question
notes.by_answer: the judge is asked with an empty slot, and asked again with the corrections made where it gave that same answer before, if there are any; the second answer stands
notes.pairs_are_cold: every request of a pair, its controls included, is sent with the server's prompt cache off, because a cached prefix can change the answer to the same prompt from one asking to the next; cold, the answer repeats, so a change between the before and the after is the correction's doing
notes.seconds: wall time of the chat-completion requests for one image as the client saw them, both requests where the judge was asked twice; in the passes over the timing images the server's prompt cache is on, after a warm-up on another image; in the pairs it is off
notes.drift: over the timing images, with every override of the part's pairs in one store; the pairs' misjudged images are left out, since their own corrections are in the slot. Indicative: one run, images in the run's order
notes.notes_are_scripted: the engineer's notes were written for this check by the unit's author looking at the crops; no engineer was involved

corrections: On a pcb1 board the judge called the flagged area 'scratch' (clause 4.2); the engineer corrected it to 'missing' (clause 4.3). The engineer's note: The transducer has lost its mesh cover: the bare metal disc shows inside the ring where the mesh should be. A part that is absent is a missing component, whatever marks the disc carries.

judgements.label: bad
judgements.judge_line: A header pin is bent out of line and leans across its neighbours.
corrections: On a pcb1 board the judge called the flagged area 'melt' (clause 4.1); the engineer corrected it to 'bent' (clause 4.4). The engineer's note: A header pin is bent out of line and leans across its neighbours. There is no solder between the pins: the bright streak is the pin's own metal.
